Chronic pancreatic insufficiency has been reported in a patient after use of rifampicin, isoniazid, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide.1 1. Liu BA, et al. Pancreatic insufficiency due to antituberculosis therapy. Ann Pharmacother 1997; 31: 724–6. Effects on the skin. Skin reactions to rifampicin are usually mild, irrespective of it being given daily or intermittently.1 How- ever, there have been a few isolated reports of severe reactions such as toxic epidermal necrolysis,2 exfoliative dermatitis,3 fixed drug eruptions,4,5 and acute generalised exanthematous pustulo- sis.6 Contact dermatitis has been seen after handling rifampicin powder.7 1. Girling DJ. Adverse reactions to rifampicin in antituberculosis regimens. J Antimicrob Chemother 1977; 3: 115–32. 2. Okano M, et al. Toxic epidermal necrolysis due to rifampicin.
